quotes.text: Attackers don't break in, they just log in, they scoop up a legitimate password through phishing, a data breach, or a simple guess, and then stroll right through the front door.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures in one image why identity has become the main attack vector.

quotes.text: Microsoft Defender for Identity is a cloud-based security tool that watches your on-premises active directory for identity-based attacks.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp one-sentence definition of the product.

quotes.text: It's not looking for malicious files. It's looking for malicious behavior. And that distinction matters because the most dangerous attacks today don't use malware at all.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the shift from malware detection to behavioral analytics.

quotes.text: A single alert might look like a false positive, but when you see the full incident, the reconnaissance, the credential compromise, the lateral movement, the domain dominance, you know exactly what happened.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows why correlated incidents beat isolated alerts.

quotes.text: If someone does log into a Honeypot account, you know immediately. Not because you set up custom monitoring, not because you wrote a complex detection rule
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the value of honeytoken accounts tangible.

chapters.title: Place in the Defender XDR ecosystem

takeaways: Defender for Identity detects identity-based attacks on on-premises Active Directory by learning normal user behavior and flagging deviations rather than scanning for malware.
Lightweight sensors on domain controllers feed a cloud service that detects reconnaissance, pass-the-hash, Kerberoasting, golden tickets, DCSync and lateral movement mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.
Combined with Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, Sentinel and Entra ID Protection inside Defender XDR, its alerts become complete attack stories.
hook: Attackers no longer break in - they log in with stolen credentials, and traditional security tools never notice. This episode explains how Microsoft Defender for Identity watches your on-premises Active Directory with sensors and behavioral analytics. Security and IT admins learn which attacks it catches and how honeytokens and Defender XDR make it even stronger.
